9 Stays in Thong Pha Phum
Kanchanaburi
We've Reviewed Each One
heroSub: 9 hand-picked stays in Thong Pha Phum district that we've already reviewed in depth — resorts on the Khwae Noi River, floating rafts near the hot springs, in-town resorts with a pool, stays by the Vajiralongkorn Dam, down to budget guesthouses by the fresh market. From about ฿600–2,100/night.
heroStats: ✅ Honest takes from real reviews, every stay
introH2: 🏞️ How many kinds of stays does Thong Pha Phum have, and how do you pick the right one for your trip?
introHtml: Thong Pha Phum is a small district in the valleys of western Kanchanaburi, the kind of place people drive through on the way to Sangkhlaburi or the waterfalls — but if you decide to spend the night, you'll find the stays here come in more shapes than you'd expect. Some are resorts on the Khwae Noi River where you wake to mist drifting over the water; some are wooden rafts floating near a hot spring that you can paddle out to and soak in; some are in-town resorts with a pool the kids can jump into; and some are budget guesthouses by the fresh market where you park right outside your door. A lot of people pick the wrong style — booking a resort far from town with no car, or expecting luxury from a few-hundred-baht stay — and end up feeling the trip wasn't what they pictured. This article rounds up 9 stays in Thong Pha Phum we've reviewed in depth — along the Khwae Noi River, by the Vajiralongkorn Dam reservoir, and in the district center. Every one comes from reading real guest reviews, telling you both the upsides and the honest caveats, comparing prices across 3 sites, and giving you direct booking links throughout.
mrtHtml: Thong Pha Phum has no skytrain and almost no public transport reaching the dam or the waterfalls — it's easiest to drive yourself or rent a car with a driver. From Kanchanaburi town it's about a 2–2.5 hour drive along Route 323, which has winding mountain stretches, so bring motion-sickness pills if you're prone to it. From Bangkok it's about 4–4.5 hours. The areas covered in this article: Thong Pha Phum town (Tha Khanun subdistrict) — easy for food, by the fresh market, walkable to Wat Tha Khanun, about 8–9 km from the Vajiralongkorn Dam. Hin Dat — on the Khwae Noi River south of the district, near the Hin Dat hot spring. Lin Thin — on the Khwae Noi River near the Lin Thin hot spring, quiet and calm. Every zone works as a base for the waterfalls, the dam, the hot springs, and onward to Sangkhlaburi.

entries.type: Resort & Spa, 3-Star · On the Khwae Noi River
entries.name: Nakakiri Resort and Spa
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Hin Dat·Thong Pha Phum · Hin Dat hot spring ~4 km
tags: ♨️ Near the Hin Dat hot spring
entries.addr: 99 Moo 1, Hin Dat, Thong Pha Phum
entries.storyHtml: If we're going to start this list with one of the stays Thong Pha Phum locals know best, plenty of reviews point to Nakakiri Resort and Spa — a large resort of about 83 rooms on the Khwae Noi River in Hin Dat subdistrict, scoring 7.7 on Trip.com and 3.5/5 on Tripadvisor from 44 reviews. What lands it at number one for us is that it's the most all-round stay in Thong Pha Phum's budget bracket — there are rooms on land, large villas, and floating rafts to choose from depending on your budget. The highlight reviews agree on most is the big outdoor pool and the separate kids' water park, where children play all day — to the point that plenty of parents say their kids won't get out of the water. Another plus that comes up often is breakfast at the Kiri restaurant, which many praise as tasty and good value, eaten riverside in the morning. The location is an advantage too, since it's only about 4 km from the Hin Dat hot spring — easy to drive over for a natural hot-spring soak and then carry on to the waterfalls. The honest caveats from the reviews: the wooden raft rooms have thin walls, so at night you hear the room next door — if you're a light sleeper, choose a villa on land or an end room. Some buildings and furnishings are starting to show their age, the menu is fairly limited if you stay several nights, and at times there are seminar groups or tour buses checked in that make the atmosphere busier than usual. The resort is about 2–2.5 hours from town and shops outside the area are far, so drive yourself and bring some food along. In short, it's best for families and groups of friends who want to swim, soak in the hot springs, and fall asleep to the sound of the river on a comfortable budget — more than for couples chasing the deepest private quiet.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you're a light sleeper, choose a villa on land or an end room instead of a raft, and ask ahead whether a seminar group will be staying during your dates. Allow time to stop at the Hin Dat hot spring and the waterfalls to make the drive worth it, and pick up food in town before heading into the resort.
pros: Most all-round in the budget bracket — rooms on land, villas, and rafts
Big pool and a separate kids' pool, children play all day
Breakfast at the Kiri restaurant, many reviews praise it as tasty and good value
About 4 km from the Hin Dat hot spring, easy to sightsee onward
cons: Thin-walled rafts, you hear the room next door (from reviews)
Some buildings showing age, limited menu over several nights
Far from town, you need your own car · busy with seminar groups at times

entries.type: Resort, 3-Star · In Thong Pha Phum town
entries.name: Keeree Loft Resort
entries.badge: 🏊 A pool in the middle of town
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Thong Pha Phum town · Vajiralongkorn Dam ~9 km
entries.addr: 233/104 Moo 1, Tha Khanun, Thong Pha Phum
entries.storyHtml: In Thong Pha Phum town, only a handful of stays have a real pool, and Keeree Loft Resort is one of them — a small 3-star resort in the middle of Thong Pha Phum town, Tha Khanun subdistrict, scoring 8.0 on Booking.com and Trip.com from 36 reviews. The reason we put it at number two is that it fits people driving around western Kanchanaburi exactly right — there's an outdoor pool and a hot tub that many reviews call larger and nicer than the price suggests for a small resort in a small town, and some name it as the reason they decided to book. The strength is the in-town location with easy food, a petrol station and convenience stores nearby, free private parking, and only about 9 km from the Vajiralongkorn Dam — under twenty minutes by car — which makes it a good base for the dam, the waterfalls, and onward to Sangkhlaburi. The staff also earn praise for being friendly and recommending places to go. The honest caveats: reviews here are fairly mixed — Booking and Trip.com give it about 8.0, but Tripadvisor is lower at around 2.5/5 from a smaller group, which reflects that the experience depends on the room you get and the timing. Some rooms and bathrooms are starting to age and could use a refresh, the Wi-Fi is slow and unstable, housekeeping is uneven at times, and there's road noise in the rooms facing outward. Breakfast is also inconsistent, so check with the resort when you book. In short, it suits people who prioritize an in-town location, a pool, and a light price over newness and a flawlessly finished room — go in with the right expectations and you'll be happy.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask to see the latest room photos and request a refreshed room or one not facing the road to avoid noise. Check on breakfast with the resort when you book, since the info differs by channel, and bring a mobile-data backup since Wi-Fi is a frequent complaint.
pros: An outdoor pool and hot tub, many reviews say better than the price
In-town location, easy food, free private parking
About 9 km from the Vajiralongkorn Dam, a good base for sightseeing
Friendly staff who recommend places to go (from reviews)
cons: Mixed reviews — Booking/Trip about 8.0 but Tripadvisor lower
Some rooms starting to age · slow, unstable Wi-Fi
Inconsistent breakfast service · road noise in outward-facing rooms

entries.type: Riverside stay · On the Vajiralongkorn Dam reservoir
entries.name: Suan Ruen Rom View Raft
entries.revCount: Wongnai 4.4/5 · Riverside stay with dam views
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Tha Khanun·Thong Pha Phum · On the Vajiralongkorn Dam reservoir
entries.storyHtml: If you've ever dreamed of opening your room door in the morning to white mist drifting over a wide stretch of water, Suan Ruen Rom View Raft is probably as close to that picture as this list gets — a riverside, nature-resort-style stay in Tha Khanun subdistrict that faces the Vajiralongkorn Dam reservoir, with the Tenasserim Range stretching out as a backdrop, scoring 4.4/5 from real reviews on Wongnai. The reason we placed it at number three despite the few reviews is that the ones it has all speak clearly and positively about the view and the quiet calm. The signature feature is rooms tiered down the hillside, every one facing the water, each with a balcony or terrace to sit and take in the full view — no room has its view blocked. The stay also offers free canoes to paddle along the water, a shallow play area for kids in the morning, and a riverside barbecue area. Prices start at about ฿2,100/night with breakfast — higher than the budget stays in town, but in exchange you get a waterfront location and a view you won't find in the district center. It's about 9 km from Wat Tha Khanun and the Vajiralongkorn Dam, convenient for sightseeing onward. The honest caveats: this is a small stay with very few reviews on the international booking platforms, and room details and prices may change with the season, so check directly with the stay on room type, number of guests, and meal packages before deciding. Because the rooms run down the hillside, some require walking up and down a slope — if walking is hard for you, ask for a room near the common area. In short, it suits couples and families who mainly want a quiet waterfront setting, a lovely view, and rest — more than people who want the full facilities of a big resort.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Contact the stay directly to confirm room type, number of guests, and meal packages before booking, since it's small and the online info isn't complete. If going up and down a slope is hard, ask for a room near the common area, and arrive before dusk to catch the sunset over the water.
pros: Views of the Vajiralongkorn Dam reservoir and the Tenasserim Range, every room faces the water
Rooms tiered down the hillside, no room's view is blocked
Free canoes and a shallow play area for kids · breakfast included
Quiet and calm, good for resting by the water, near Wat Tha Khanun and the dam
cons: Small stay, few reviews on international platforms, check directly
Rooms run down the hillside, some require walking up and down a slope
Pricier than in-town stays · facilities not as complete as a big resort

entries.type: Riverside raft resort, 2-Star · On the Khwae Noi River
entries.name: Mek Kiri Riverkwai Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Tha Khanun·Thong Pha Phum · Hin Dat hot spring ~7 km
tags: ♨️ Near the Hin Dat hot spring
entries.addr: 24 Moo 2, Tha Kha-nun, Thong Pha Phum
entries.storyHtml: For anyone who wants to actually try sleeping on a floating wooden raft without paying a lot, Mek Kiri Riverkwai Resort is a small raft resort on the Khwae Noi River in Thong Pha Phum district, about 260 km from Bangkok, scoring around 7.2 from real reviews on Booking.com and Trip.com. Many reviews call it a stay for people who want to cut off from the chaos and rest quietly by the river in nature, more than to find luxury or a full set of facilities. The image reviews agree on is opening the raft-room door in the morning to mist over the river with a line of green mountains behind, swinging in a riverside hammock and feeding the fish — and at times there's a morning alms-giving on the raft, an atmosphere you won't get in the city. The star here is the Raft Room, a wooden room floating on the river with a balcony jutting over the water, while those on a tighter budget have the Garden View rooms on land at a lighter price. The location is about 7 km from the Hin Dat hot spring, so you can drive over for a soak. The honest caveats: it's a small 2-star resort with basic facilities and no pool, so anyone expecting an all-round resort may be disappointed. The wooden raft rooms don't block sound well, by the nature of a raft, so you hear the next room and the water. It's far from town and shops, so drive yourself and bring food along. In short, it suits couples and groups of friends who want a quiet raft-by-the-river experience on a budget and are willing to trade full facilities for genuine nature.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you're set on sleeping on a raft, book the Raft Room directly, since it's the star here and limited in number. Bring food and supplies along since shops are far, and allow time to stop at the Hin Dat hot spring about 7 km away.
pros: A floating wooden raft experience on the Khwae Noi River on a budget
Quiet nature, mountain views, riverside hammocks
Rooms on land at a lighter price if your budget is tight
About 7 km from the Hin Dat hot spring, easy to sightsee onward
cons: Small 2-star resort, no pool, basic facilities
Wooden raft rooms don't block sound, you hear the next room and the water
Far from town and shops, you need your own car

entries.name: Cinque Terre Resort
entries.badge: 🏡 Italian-style design · Quiet, near a stream
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Tha Khanun·Thong Pha Phum · ~4–5 km from the district center
entries.addr: 266/99 Moo 4, Tha Kha-nun, Thong Pha Phum
entries.storyHtml: If you want a Thong Pha Phum stay that doesn't look like anywhere else, Cinque Terre Resort is a small resort of just a few buildings deliberately styled to evoke the seaside village of Cinque Terre in Italy, in Tha Khanun subdistrict, about 4–5 km from Thong Pha Phum town, scoring 7.2 on Trip.com. The reason we put it in the middle of the list is that it has its own charm in design and quiet, but it's a small stay with few reviews, so we've gathered the honest voices we could find, both praise and criticism. The selling point is the bright European-style buildings, rooms larger than the price, a small garden, a stream or little weir running out back, and a quiet area to walk that an in-town resort can't give you. There's a barbecue area, free parking, and it's a pet-friendly stay — not common in this zone — so it fits people who want to bring the dog or cat along. It works as a base for the waterfalls, the national parks, and the viewpoints around Thong Pha Phum and Sangkhlaburi. The honest caveats: because the reviews are still very few, set your expectations at a small, homey stay rather than an international-standard resort. It's on the district outskirts, so you have to drive out for food — you can't walk to a convenience store. There's no pool, and in some seasons there may be insects from the surrounding nature, as at any stay near a stream. In short, it suits couples or small groups who like an unusual-looking, quiet stay, can bring pets, and want a base for driving around — more than families who need a pool and full facilities.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Since it's a small stay with few reviews, ask about the latest room condition and food service before booking. If bringing a pet, let them know in advance, and pick up food in town before heading in, since it's on the outskirts.
pros: Unusual Italian-style design, rooms larger than the price
Quiet, with a garden and a small stream out back
Pet-friendly · barbecue area and free parking
Light starting price, good as a base for driving around
cons: Small stay, still very few reviews, ask before booking
On the district outskirts, you drive out for food · no pool
Some seasons may bring insects from the nearby stream

entries.type: Budget riverside stay, 2-Star · In the district center
entries.name: Thongphaphum River
entries.badge: 🏞️ Riverside in town · Best value on the Khwae
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Thong Pha Phum·Tha Khanun · Wat Tha Khanun ~2 km
entries.storyHtml: If you drive up the mountain into Thong Pha Phum in the evening and want a clean, affordable stay in the district center, within walking distance of convenience stores and restaurants, Thongphaphum River is the answer many reviews call good value — a small riverside stay of just 16 rooms in Tha Khanun subdistrict, scoring around 8.3 from 53 reviews on Trip.com and 7.5 on Booking.com. The reason we placed it here is that it delivers exactly what it says in the budget riverside bracket — clean rooms with air-con, a TV, a fridge, and a balcony to relax on, starting at only about ฿750/night, the cheapest among the riverside stays on this list. The location is in the district center, a few steps from the bank of the Khwae River, about 2 km from Wat Tha Khanun, near the Vajiralongkorn Dam and the Hin Dat hot spring — good as a base for nature trips, then back to sleep in town with easy food. There's a 24-hour front desk, luggage storage, free Wi-Fi, and free private parking. The honest caveats: this isn't a large luxury raft resort on the river but a simple stay focused on being clean and good value, with no pool. With only 16 rooms it fills up fast on long weekends, so book ahead. Some rooms are by the road and may get passing traffic noise. In short, it suits couples, small families, and travelers who prioritize cleanliness, an in-town location, and a light price over a full riverside-resort atmosphere.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: With only 16 rooms and good value, it fills fast on long weekends, so book ahead and compare across 3 sites. If you're sensitive to noise, ask for a room away from the road, and use the in-town advantage to walk out for meals and shopping.
pros: Prices start in the hundreds, cheapest among the riverside stays on the list
16 clean rooms with air-con, TV, fridge, and a balcony to relax on
In the district center, walk to the Khwae River, easy food
24-hour front desk · free Wi-Fi and parking
cons: Not a full riverside resort · no pool
Only 16 rooms, fills fast on long weekends, book ahead
Some rooms by the road may get traffic noise (from reviews)

entries.type: Homestay/riverside raft, 3-Star · On the Khwae Noi River
entries.name: Baan Rai Darun Home Stay and Scenery Raft
entries.revCount: Trip.com 8.7 · #1 specialty stay in Lin Thin (Tripadvisor)
entries.badge: ♨️ Raft out to soak in the Lin Thin hot spring
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Lin Thin·Thong Pha Phum · Lin Thin hot spring 420 m

rooms.type: Floating raft room, sleep to the sound of water (breakfast included)

tags: ♨️ 420 m from the Lin Thin hot spring
🛶 Raft, sleep to the sound of water
entries.addr: 21/16 Moo 2, Lin Thin, Thong Pha Phum
entries.storyHtml: If there's one stay on this list that sells an experience you'd struggle to find elsewhere, many reviews point to Baan Rai Darun Home Stay and Scenery Raft — a stay on the Khwae Noi River in Lin Thin subdistrict, scoring 8.7/10 from real reviews on Trip.com and ranked the number-one specialty stay in Lin Thin on Tripadvisor. What people talk about most is that it's only 420 m from the Lin Thin hot spring, close enough that you can float out on a raft to soak in the hot water and drift back with the current — something almost no other stay can do. The main atmosphere is sleeping on a net-floored raft on the Khwae Noi River, listening to the water flow all night, and waking to views of the Thong Pha Phum mountains. There are several options by budget, from a studio room with a large bed and a river or mountain view starting around ฿1,500, a floating raft room around ฿3,000, up to a large 2-bedroom house for families — and every option includes breakfast, with some packages including dinner. There are wet-rafting trips, cycling, and riverside barbecue. The honest caveats: it's a small homestay-style stay with still-few reviews on the international platforms, so set your expectations at warm and homey rather than hotel standard. It's deep in Lin Thin, so you have to drive yourself and shops are far — bring supplies along. The raft rooms and waterside areas mean you should be careful with small children near the water. In short, it suits couples and families who want a distinctive riverside experience — sleeping on a raft, floating out to the hot spring, and resting quietly — more than people who want the full facilities of a big resort.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The selling point is rafting out to the Lin Thin hot spring, so ask the stay about the raft trips and meal packages when you book. It's a small homestay, so book ahead and drive yourself since it's deep in, shops are far, and watch small children closely since the stay is by the water.
pros: 420 m from the Lin Thin hot spring, raft out to soak and drift back
A net-floored raft experience on the Khwae Noi River, the sound of water all night
Several options by budget, all include breakfast
#1 specialty stay in Lin Thin on Tripadvisor (from reviews)
cons: Small homestay, still few reviews on international platforms
Deep in Lin Thin, you need your own car, shops are far
Raft rooms and waterside areas, watch small children near the water

entries.type: Budget guesthouse, 2-Star · Middle of the district
entries.name: Thongphaphum Place
entries.badge: 💰 Cheapest on the list · By the fresh market
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Central Thong Pha Phum · By the fresh market and 7-Eleven
entries.addr: 108/5 Moo 1, Tha Khanun, Thong Pha Phum
entries.storyHtml: For anyone on the tightest budget who sees a stay as just a place to lay your head between driving trips, Thongphaphum Place is a small budget guesthouse of just 9 rooms in the middle of Thong Pha Phum town, Tha Khanun subdistrict, that real reviews call one of the most value-for-money and cleanest in-town stays, with an average score around 8.5 across platforms. The reason we put it late in the list isn't because it's not good, but because it's a different style from the riverside stays above — this is a purely in-town stay that sells convenience and price, not a view or a nature setting. The strength is a starting price of only about ฿600/night, the cheapest on this list, with clean rooms that many reviews say are recently renovated, air-con, an LCD TV, free drinking water, and daily cleaning. The location is the real star — by the fresh market and a 7-Eleven, so you park out front and walk over for food in a few steps, walkable to Wat Tha Khanun and the bus station, about 8 km from the Vajiralongkorn Dam. There's a 24-hour front desk, luggage storage, free Wi-Fi, and free parking, good for arriving late or leaving early. The honest caveats: it's a small 2-star guesthouse with simple, functional rooms, no pool or resort-style facilities. With only 9 rooms it fills fast, so book ahead. It's by the market and the road, so it's lively in the morning and may get some noise. In short, it suits budget travelers, traveling pairs, and people using Thong Pha Phum as an overnight stop before heading up to Sangkhlaburi, who want a clean stay, a convenient location, and a light price more than a restful riverside atmosphere.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: With only 9 rooms and low prices, it fills fast, so book ahead, especially on long weekends. Use the by-the-market advantage to grab food in the morning before heading out, and if you're sensitive to noise, ask for a room away from the road or toward the back.
pros: Starts at about ฿600/night, the cheapest on the list
Clean rooms that many reviews say are recently renovated
By the fresh market and 7-Eleven, walkable to Wat Tha Khanun
24-hour check-in · free Wi-Fi and parking
cons: Small 2-star guesthouse, no pool or resort-style facilities
Only 9 rooms, fills fast, book ahead
By the market and the road, lively in the morning and may get noise

entries.name: Puprai Tarnnarm Resort
entries.badge: 🌳 Wide 70-rai grounds · Next to a zipline park
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Tha Khanun·Thong Pha Phum · Next to a zipline adventure park
entries.addr: 242/5 Moo 1, Tha Khanun, Thong Pha Phum
entries.storyHtml: We close the list with a stay that mainly sells "space" — Puprai Tarnnarm Resort is a resort on the Khwae Noi River set on about 70 rai of land in Tha Khanun subdistrict, scoring 7.5 from 39 reviews on Trip.com and 4.0/5 on Tripadvisor (#1 B&B in Thong Pha Phum). What sets it apart from the other stays on the list is the wide-open grounds stretching as far as you can see — a big lawn, the Khwae Noi River flowing out front, and the Thong Pha Phum mountains as a backdrop, in a way an in-town resort can't give you. There's an outdoor pool, a riverside activity area, a kids' play area, a picnic area, a garden cafe, and bicycle and kayak rentals. The highlight that draws groups of friends and families is that it sits next to the Puprai Adventure Park zipline park, and it's within driving distance of the Hin Dat hot spring, Pha Sawan Waterfall, and Khao Laem National Park. A particularly good value is the large 7–8 bedroom house, which works out very cheap per head for large groups and seminar groups, while couples or small families have the Superior and river-view studio rooms starting around ฿800. The honest caveats from the reviews: because the grounds are large and fairly old, upkeep and cleanliness are uneven in places, and some furnishings are starting to age. At times with large groups or group activities checked in, the atmosphere gets lively and noisy — if you're after quiet, check the dates first. Wi-Fi only covers the common areas, and it's about 2.5–3 hours from town, so you need a car. In short, it's best for large families, groups of friends, and parties who want wide-open space, swimming, outdoor activities, and ziplining — more than couples chasing a polished, private quiet.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you're coming as a large group, ask about the 7–8 bedroom house, since it works out very cheap per head. Allow time to zipline at the adventure park next to the resort and stop at the Hin Dat hot spring, and if you're after quiet, check first whether a large group or group activity is staying during your dates.
pros: Wide grounds of about 70 rai on the Khwae Noi River, open and airy
Has a pool, an activity area, bicycle and kayak rentals
Next to a zipline adventure park · near the Hin Dat hot spring
7–8 bedroom house, cheap per head for large groups
cons: Wide and fairly old grounds, cleanliness uneven in places
At times with large groups/activities, the atmosphere is lively and noisy
Wi-Fi only in common areas · far from town, you need a car

adviceTitle: How do you pick a stay in Thong Pha Phum to match your trip?

advice.head: A family bringing kids to swim, wanting a pool
advice.bodyHtml: → Nakakiri Resort and Spa ฿900, a big pool + kids' pool on the Khwae Noi River, or Puprai Tarnnarm Resort ฿800, 70 rai of grounds with a pool and zipline

advice.head: Wanting to try sleeping on a floating wooden raft by the river
advice.bodyHtml: → Mek Kiri Riverkwai Resort ฿1,200, a floating wooden raft with riverside hammocks on a budget, or Baan Rai Darun ฿1,500, a raft you sleep on to the sound of water that you can float out to the hot spring from

advice.head: Wanting a lovely view by the dam, quiet and calm
advice.bodyHtml: → Suan Ruen Rom View Raft ฿2,100, rooms tiered down the hillside, views of the Vajiralongkorn Dam reservoir and the Tenasserim Range, breakfast included

advice.head: Wanting hot-spring soaking as the main activity
advice.bodyHtml: → Baan Rai Darun ฿1,500, raft out to the Lin Thin hot spring 420 m away, or Nakakiri / Mek Kiri, both near the Hin Dat hot spring

advice.head: Wanting a pool but staying in town
advice.bodyHtml: → Keeree Loft Resort ฿1,200, one of the few stays in Thong Pha Phum town with an outdoor pool and a hot tub, near the Vajiralongkorn Dam

advice.head: Tightest budget, just a place to lay your head
advice.bodyHtml: → Thongphaphum Place ฿600 by the fresh market, or Thongphaphum River ฿750 riverside in town — both clean and in-town

advice.head: Wanting to bring a pet, or liking unusual design
advice.bodyHtml: → Cinque Terre Resort ฿900, a small Italian-style resort, pet-friendly, quiet near a stream, on the district outskirts

noteHtml: 📌 Note: All prices are approximate starting rates from the standard-room range and may change by date and season; we recommend checking the real price and comparing 3 sites before every booking. The scores and highlights in this article come from reading real guest reviews on the booking platforms (Trip.com / Booking.com / Tripadvisor / Wongnai); we did not stay ourselves. Many stays in Thong Pha Phum are small (9–16 rooms, some are homestays), so they fill fast and reviews are still few — book ahead and ask the stay directly about room types and meal packages. Over long weekends and the cool season (Nov–Feb), stays fill fast and prices rise, so book ahead. Thong Pha Phum has almost no public transport reaching the dam and the waterfalls — we recommend driving yourself, about 2–2.5 hours from Kanchanaburi town and about 4–4.5 hours from Bangkok. faqTitle: FAQ — common questions travelers ask about staying in Thong Pha Phum

faq.q: ❓ What's the best place to stay in Thong Pha Phum?
faq.a: It depends on your trip style. For a family bringing kids to swim, Nakakiri Resort and Spa has a big pool and is the most all-round in the budget bracket. If you want a pool but staying in town, Keeree Loft Resort. If you're focused on quiet dam views, Suan Ruen Rom View Raft, scoring 4.4/5 on Wongnai. If you want to sleep on a raft and soak in a hot spring, Baan Rai Darun. And if you're on the tightest budget, Thongphaphum Place from ฿600, the cheapest on the list.

faq.q: ❓ How much do stays in Thong Pha Phum cost?
faq.a: In this article, prices start at about ฿600–2,100 per night. The most budget-friendly are Thongphaphum Place from ฿600 and Thongphaphum River from ฿750. The riverside resorts with a pool start at about ฿800–1,500 (Puprai, Nakakiri, Keeree Loft, Mek Kiri, Cinque Terre, Baan Rai Darun). Suan Ruen Rom View Raft starts at about ฿2,100 with breakfast. All prices are approximate starting rates from standard rooms; over long weekends they may run higher than usual.

faq.q: ❓ Which zone is best in Thong Pha Phum, in town or by the river?
faq.a: In the district center (Tha Khanun subdistrict) suits people driving around who want easy food and a base for the dam and waterfalls (Keeree Loft, Thongphaphum River, Thongphaphum Place). On the Khwae Noi River (Hin Dat/Tha Khanun/Lin Thin) suits people who want a riverside nature setting and sleeping to the sound of water (Nakakiri, Mek Kiri, Baan Rai Darun, Puprai). On the Vajiralongkorn Dam reservoir suits people focused on wide views and quiet (Suan Ruen Rom View Raft). Every zone is best with your own car.

faq.q: ❓ Which stays in Thong Pha Phum are near a hot spring?
faq.a: Thong Pha Phum has 2 popular hot springs. Near the Hin Dat hot spring: Nakakiri Resort and Spa (~4 km) and Mek Kiri Riverkwai Resort (~7 km). Near the Lin Thin hot spring: Baan Rai Darun, only 420 m away and notable for letting you float out on a raft to soak in the hot water and drift back with the current — an experience that's hard to find elsewhere.

faq.q: ❓ Which stays in Thong Pha Phum suit families and large groups?
faq.a: Families bringing kids to swim suit Nakakiri Resort and Spa (big pool + kids' pool) and Puprai Tarnnarm Resort (70 rai of grounds with a pool and zipline). For large groups or seminar groups, we recommend Puprai Tarnnarm, with a 7–8 bedroom house that's good value per head, and Nakakiri, with a meeting room for groups. For both, check first whether another group is staying during your dates if you want quiet.

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should you book a stay in Thong Pha Phum · how do you get there?
faq.a: Most stays in Thong Pha Phum are small (9–16 rooms, some are homestays or have just a few buildings), so they fill fast. Over long weekends and the cool season (Nov–Feb), book 2–4 weeks ahead or more, and most platforms offer Free Cancellation — we recommend locking in a rate that way if your plans aren't firm, then comparing Agoda / Booking / Trip.com. On getting there: Thong Pha Phum has almost no public transport reaching the dam and the waterfalls, so drive yourself or rent a car with a driver, about 2–2.5 hours from Kanchanaburi town and about 4–4.5 hours from Bangkok.
